heroHeadline: SpaceX Launches Historic $1.77 Trillion IPO Roadshow — Amazon Leo Reaches 331 Satellites as ViaTunisia Cable Links North Africa to Europe
heroSubtitle: SpaceX set its IPO roadshow price at $135/share on June 3, 2026, implying a $1.77 trillion valuation — history's largest IPO — with Starlink's role connecting 2.6 billion unconnected people at the center of the investment case. Amazon Leo (formerly Project Kuiper) launched its LA-07 mission on May 29, bringing its constellation to 331 satellites as it races toward its FCC July 30 milestone of 1,618 in orbit. The ViaTunisia subsea cable reached Ready for Service on June 3, establishing the first EU-funded direct high-capacity link between France and Tunisia. India's TRAI and Broadband India Forum pushed in early June to formally recognize Public Wi-Fi as a core broadband infrastructure layer alongside fiber and 5G — critical for achieving the National Broadband Mission 2.0 target of 270,000 villages. The African Digital Week Forum in Abidjan (June 1–2) highlighted Côte d'Ivoire's 6,632 km fiber backbone as a replicable West Africa model.
footerNote: Data sourced from ITU, GSMA, World Bank, A4AI, SpaceX IPO prospectus, Amazon Leo filings, NTIA/FCC, and major international research outlets. Contested figures noted with confidence levels.
